title: Double the side, quadruple area
hook: Two square surfaces have side lengths 2m and 4m. Is the second only twice as large?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Apply square scaling to area coverage.

misconception: Doubling a square’s side only doubles the area to cover.
objective: Apply square scaling to area coverage.

claims.text: Compare an ideal square of side 2m with one of side 4m. B’s side remains twice A’s. Scaled model; ideal squares; area=side×side.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Side=2m, A=4m² and B=16m². The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x","x"]; B=["*",2,"x",2,"x"]; x denotes Side. At x=2, A=4, B=16; recall at x=5: B=100. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Both dimensions double, so the product gets a factor of two twice. Four times the area means four times the material in an ideal area-only coverage model, rather than twice.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x","x"]; B=["*",2,"x",2,"x"]; x denotes Side. At x=2, A=4, B=16; recall at x=5: B=100. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: Compare an ideal square of side 2m with one of side 4m. B’s side remains twice A’s. Change only Side to 5m. What is B (Side-2x) now? Correct: 100m². Use B's stated rule with Side=5m: it gives 100m². Both dimensions double, so the product gets a factor of two twice. Four times the area means four times the material in an ideal area-only coverage model, rather than twice.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x","x"]; B=["*",2,"x",2,"x"]; x denotes Side. At x=2, A=4, B=16; recall at x=5: B=100. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

recall.question: Compare an ideal square of side 2m with one of side 4m. B’s side remains twice A’s. Change only Side to 5m. What is B (Side-2x) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Side=5m: it gives 100m². Both dimensions double, so the product gets a factor of two twice. Four times the area means four times the material in an ideal area-only coverage model, rather than twice.

safety.assumptions: Compare an ideal square of side 2m with one of side 4m. B’s side remains twice A’s.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
